summary.text: Jim Himes is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2008.
Before politics he worked in finance at Goldman Sachs and in affordable-housing finance at Enterprise Community Partners, and he held local office in Greenwich.
In Congress he is the ranking member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and also serves on the House Financial Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Himes was born in Lima, Peru, in 1966 to American parents.
According to his official biography, he spent his early childhood in Peru and Colombia, where his father worked for the Ford Foundation and UNICEF, and moved to the United States at age ten.
He graduated from Hopewell Valley Central High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Harvard University in 1988 and, as a Rhodes Scholar, a master's degree from Oxford University in 1990.
Himes began his career at Goldman Sachs, where over a 12-year career he rose to vice president, worked extensively in Latin America and headed the bank's telecommunications technology group.

He later ran the New York City branch of Enterprise Community Partners, a nonprofit focused on urban poverty, whose team financed thousands of affordable housing units in the New York metropolitan region.

In Greenwich, Himes chaired the Greenwich Housing Authority from 2003 to 2006 and served on the town's board of estimate and taxation from 2006 to 2007; he has also chaired the Greenwich Democratic Town Committee.
He was first elected to the U.S. House in 2008 and took office in 2009, succeeding Republican Chris Shays, and is serving his ninth term.
Himes serves as ranking member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and sits on the House Financial Services Committee.
According to his official biography, Himes lives in Greenwich with his wife, Mary, and has two daughters.
